meta_description:
6,086 likes, 6,069 comments - luke_coutinho on October 8, 2026: "One of the biggest misconceptions about fasting is that eating less automatically means you're doing something good for your body.

But that's not always the case.

Over the years, I've seen how easily fasting can turn into a routine of long gaps between meals, very little protein, and then one heavy meal at the end of the day.

And sometimes, we don't even realise it.

We feel tired, experience cravings, struggle with digestion, or find ourselves reaching for something sweet just to get through the day.

Now, fasting has a beautiful place in our traditions. It's a time for devotion, discipline, reflection, and connecting with something deeper.

And I believe we can respect that while also respecting our body's physiology.

Here's something worth understanding.

Fasting and nourishment are not opposites.

You don't necessarily have to eat large quantities to nourish yourself well. What matters is how you put your meals together, the quality of your ingredients, and whether you're giving your body what it needs.

For example, instead of making your fasting meals entirely carbohydrate-based, you can explore combinations that offer a better balance of nutrients.

You can also experiment with different ways of preparing familiar fasting ingredients. A few thoughtful additions or swaps can make your meals more satisfying without making your time in the kitchen complicated.

And remember, there's no single way to fast.

Some people follow one meal a day. Others eat several smaller meals using permitted ingredients. Some avoid particular foods, while others follow different family traditions.

Your nutritional needs will also depend on your age, activity levels, health conditions, and the type of fast you're observing.

The goal is not to make fasting another stressful diet or a competition in restriction.

It's to find a rhythm that honours your beliefs and supports your well-being.

We've put together some simple Navratri fasting meal options that you can choose from, adapt, and include according to your preferences and traditions.

Small choices can make a meaningful difference.

💚 Comment “NAVRATRI” and our team will send you our free Nourishing Navratri guide.".
